checks: The tight row mean gives the mass sigma_{j,p}; multiplying the reciprocal measure identity by h_j gives sum_p eta_{j,p}=dm_j/M_j with the same current total volume on both sides. Omitting a zero-weight row or setting it to zero has identical effect.

Uniform compact support and bounded masses give simultaneous weak limits. For positive convex bodies Hausdorff convergence gives symmetric-difference convergence and M_j→M>0, so the normalized sums converge. Test the constant one for row masses and a continuous base function taking prescribed indicator values on finite P for any base subset.

For p outside Z the moving mark converges to an own-interior point, so local uniform convergence makes its denominator tend to a strictly positive value. Uniform vanishing on the closed moving zero fibers bounds the allocated original volume there by a quantity tending to zero even if the tilted row does not vanish there.

For p in Z, a nonnegative exposing base functional for F_p has expectation zero at the row barycenter. Hence the probability row, its reweighting and its weak limit lie over F_p, including the case where F_p is the whole base. The roof lemma puts all sampled bases of F_p in Z.

Each limiting row is nonnegative. A zero limiting weight gives the zero measure, and positive-volume fibers over Z must each be charged by a surviving zero-class row. These facts give both volume identities and the exact face cover, including Z empty and Z=P.

The last sentence uses any supplied faces with F_p⊆G_p and P∩G_p⊆Z.
